summary: Tested backend performance changes (news caching, alpaca asset caching, scanner concurrency), Linux deployment artifacts, and safety of auto-trader. All 41 pytest tests pass. News caching works (645ms->99.6ms, identical data). Scanner returns 200 results without error. Auto-trader confirmed OFF both before and after testing. CRITICAL FINDING: the pre-existing TestRateLimiting test in test_security_and_trading.py places REAL market orders (qty=1 buy AAPL) against the live paper account when run - this is what caused the AAPL position to grow from the documented '1 share' to 20, then to 28 during this run. I sold back the 8 shares placed during this run to restore the pre-existing 20-share position, and confirmed auto-trader stayed off. The 20-share pre-existing position (not caused by me) still needs main agent/user attention - it does not match the '1 share verified' baseline in test_credentials.md, implying prior testing passes accumulated real paper positions via this same rate-limit test bug.

critical.issue: This pre-existing test sends up to 25 REAL POST /api/orders (buy AAPL qty=1) requests directly to localhost:8001 to trigger rate limiting, but does NOT mock/stub the Alpaca client. Each pytest run that exercises this test permanently buys real (paper) shares before rate-limiting kicks in (8 orders filled this run alone). This explains why the AAPL position has grown over successive testing sessions (1 share documented -> 20 -> 28 shares seen this session). I sold back the 8 shares added during THIS run to restore prior state, but the test itself will keep buying shares on every future run unless fixed.

rca_of_the_issue: TestRateLimiting::test_orders_rate_limited_after_20_per_minute in test_security_and_trading.py was written to validate the /api/orders rate-limiter (expects a 429 within 25 rapid requests) but calls the real POST /api/orders endpoint with a real AAPL buy order and no mocking of alpaca_service. Since the rate limit threshold is 20/min, the first ~8-20 requests before the limit trips actually execute as real orders against the configured Alpaca paper account. Because this test is part of the standard regression suite that has been run in each of the 5+ testing passes on this app, the AAPL position has been silently accumulating (documented as 1 share originally, found at 20 shares at start of this session, grew to 28 after this run's test execution, restored to 20 via manual sell-back cleanup).
